_comment: Maps Wikipedia poll-table column headers to the party ids used in index.html. Edit this file — not the Python — when a party renames, merges, or appears. Any Wikipedia column not listed here, and any app party with no column, is reported as a WARNING by fetch_polls.py and fails the GitHub Action, so a new party can never be silently dropped.

headline._comment: The headline seat numbers come from one pollster commissioned by one outlet. strict_publisher=true means ONLY Kantar polls for Kan 11 count, so the seat series and its change arrows compare like with like. Kan 11 commissions Kantar weekly. Set strict_publisher=false to take the newest Kantar poll whatever the outlet (fresher, but mixes two sample series).

_spread_comment: Per-party min-max range is computed across ALL pollsters within this many days of the headline poll, so the 'spread' text stays honest even though the headline is one house.

app_parties_without_column.balad: Wikipedia reports a single 'Joint List' column; Balad is not polled separately. Decide editorially whether Balad still runs alone.

_cycle_comment: The page also carries hypothetical-scenario tables and tables from previous election cycles. Only the main chronological tables carry a 'Samplesize' column, so a table must have that AND every column listed here (exact header match) to be read. If the field realigns and a lead party renames, update this list.
_history_comment: How far back to read. Bounds ingestion to the tables covering the current party lineup — older tables list parties that no longer exist and would only add noise. Must be comfortably larger than spread_window_days so the previous same-house poll (for the delta arrows) is still in range.
_trend_comment: How far back the per-party sparkline reaches (9 weeks). Tables older than history_days are read leniently for this — their columns are parties that have since merged or folded, and an unrecognised one simply contributes no trend point rather than failing the run. The trend uses the headline house only, so it is one consistent series.
_alternates_comment: How many recent polls to offer in the reader's poll picker. Only polls measuring every party on the board are included, so the totals stay at 120 and no party shows a zero its pollster never tested.
_exclude_comment: Pollsters to keep out of the reader's poll picker entirely. Leave empty to show them with a note instead — excluding a house reads as removing the numbers you dislike, whereas disclosing who owns it lets the reader judge. Names must match the 'Polling firm' column.

pollster_notes.Filber: Channel 14 established and owns this polling firm, and aired its polls without disclosing that; Israel's Public Council for Press and Ethics said it may constitute a breach of public trust.

_notes_comment: Shown under the picker when that pollster's poll is selected, after the measured house effect. Keep it to what arithmetic cannot say — who owns the firm, who commissions it — and let the lean figure carry the numbers. Avoid labels like 'aligned' or 'mainstream': they are contestable in a way an ownership fact and a seat count are not.
_lean_comment: House effect is measured on this bloc's seat total: each pollster's 30-day average minus the median across every poll, in seats. Keep it in step with the blocs on the board.
